sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Novi
sections.html:
Novi owners usually choose between a full-service listing, a private sale, and a quick sale to a buyer who pays without a bank. Every route ends in the same two places: the city Assessing Department for tax forms, and the Oakland County deed office for the transfer.

The routes differ in timing and in what comes out of your pocket. Showings, a buyer's loan approval and repair negotiations can stretch a listing across months. A direct purchase squeezes that into one negotiation. Ask each buyer for the net amount you would receive and compare those figures side by side. The local steps below apply no matter which route you pick.

Novi is a northwestern Detroit suburb in Oakland County, roughly 25 miles from downtown Detroit, and home values here run high. Interstates 96, 696 and 275 meet in the city and M-5 adds another link, so a house near one of those roads is a short drive from much of metro Detroit.

Owners who carry a mortgage pay about $2,495 a month at the middle of the range, against $915 for owners with no mortgage. These are citywide numbers. A sold listing on your own street tells you more about your price than any of them do.

Novi Community Schools covers most of the city. Northville Public Schools takes in a large part of the south side, Walled Lake Consolidated Schools has a pocket, and South Lyon Community Schools reaches a small strip at the west edge. The district tied to a specific address often decides which buyers call, so confirm it with the schools before you print it in a listing.

Shopping along Haggerty Road and Grand River Avenue, the Twelve Oaks Mall area and a large hospital campus all keep the city busy. Relocating employees from out of state and overseas are part of the buyer pool, since 29.2% of residents are foreign-born and 33.2% of residents aged five and up speak another language at home.

sections.h2: Assessing department forms at a sale
sections.html:
The Novi Assessing Department answers at 248-347-0485 and handles four items you will likely touch at a sale.

  • Transfer affidavit: state law wants it filed within 45 days after the date of transfer.
  • Principal residence exemption: this takes up to 18 mills of school operating tax off a homeowner's bill. When the house sells, file the rescission form right away, because penalties and interest run back to the sale date if filing is late.
  • Conditional rescission: someone who moved into a new Michigan home can keep a conditional rescission on the old one for up to three years, as long as the old house is listed, empty, unrented and unused for business.
  • Board of Review: an assessment protest starts with a petition to the board.

City appraisers walk neighborhoods every year, and the State Tax Commission suggests that assessors inspect 20% of parcels annually, refreshing photos and sometimes measuring. A new deck, finished basement or garage will show up on the record card. Owners with low incomes can ask for a hardship exemption at the July or December board, bringing two years of returns and current account statements.

Buyers and their inspectors ask about work done to the house, so permit history matters. Novi publishes separate applications for building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work, and an owner acting as general contractor completes the Homeowner Permit Policy form.

There is also an occupancy request form for new construction, and the Building Department needs two days' notice to process it. A temporary certificate of occupancy runs through the Administrative Board of Appeals. If you pulled permits for a kitchen, furnace, roof or addition, collect the final inspection sign-offs now. A change that affects drainage, such as a regraded yard or new patio, needs a Minor Land Improvement Permit, so check your records for one. The Novi Building Department can supply a copy of any record you cannot locate.

sections.h2: Recording at the Oakland County deed office
sections.html:
The transfer is recorded at the Oakland County Register of Deeds, reachable at 248-858-0597. Recording a deed costs $30.00, a total that folds in a $4 state land-survey charge.

Any deed with a warranty covenant has to be tax certified at the Oakland County Treasurer's Office before recording, for a $5.00 certificate charge. The closing agent usually walks both steps over. Pages need a 2-1/2 inch blank strip at the top and a half inch elsewhere.

Transfer tax is 55 cents for each $500 of consideration to the county and $3.75 for each $500 to the state. Look for both lines on your closing statement before you sign.

A few days of prep shortens the whole sale. Pull your last deed, gather permit sign-offs and any receipts for a roof or furnace, and ask Assessing which exemption forms you need to file. Then decide who in your closing team handles the transfer affidavit and the county filing so nothing is skipped or filed twice.

A buyer paying without a loan may take the house as it stands, while a lender behind a financed buyer can insist on fixes. Knowing which kind of buyer you have shapes how much repair work is worth doing at all.

A cash buyer has no lender, so there is no appraisal waiting on a bank and no loan approval that can fall through at the last minute. Repairs are negotiated once, in the offer, instead of again after the buyer's inspection. You still need the county recording, the tax certificate for a warranty deed and the assessor forms, so a cash sale shortens the calendar but does not remove the paperwork.

When you compare offers, ask each buyer who pays for the recording, the certificate and the transfer tax. Put the answers in writing before you sign, and confirm the numbers against your closing statement. If you moved out and still hold a principal residence exemption on the old house, the rescission form should go in the same week the sale closes.

faqs.q: Do Novi sellers have to fix things before closing?
faqs.a: No Novi rule forces repairs before a sale. Unpermitted or unfinished work is the exception, so ask the Building Department about permit history first. A buyer paying without a loan may take the house as it stands, while a lender behind a financed buyer can insist on fixes.

faqs.q: When is the Property Transfer Affidavit due after a Novi sale?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the transfer. It goes to the city assessor, and your closing agent may be able to submit it for you.

faqs.q: Does the principal residence exemption stay with the house after a Novi sale?
faqs.a: No. The seller must rescind it with the assessor as soon as the home is sold, rented or left, and late filing triggers penalties and interest back to that date. A conditional rescission can last up to three years on a vacant, listed, unrented former home.

faqs.q: Which office takes the deed after a Novi closing?
faqs.a: The Oakland County Register of Deeds, not the city. Recording costs $30.00, and a warranty deed first needs a $5.00 treasurer's tax certificate, so most sellers leave the filing to their closing agent.

faqs.q: Which school district will a Novi buyer be in?
faqs.a: Most of Novi is in Novi Community Schools. The south side is in Northville Public Schools, a section is in Walled Lake Consolidated Schools and a small western piece is in South Lyon Community Schools, so check the district for your address.
